rationale: The registry unit wv-dui-deferral-unit-2-application-to-expunge declares outputStrategy 'custom_pleading', outputStrategyStatus 'resolved', packetIdentity 'identified' and available true, and the corresponding packetSet component carries no officialFormId.

SCA-C903, SCA-C906 and SCA-C907 are the West Virginia expungement instruments, and all three are § 61-11-25 or § 61-11-26 filings. Using one here would put the participant into the conviction route, where § 61-11-26b expressly bars expunging DUI convictions.

The relief is mandatory on a stated finding — if objections are filed and the court determines there was no serious or repeated violation of the conditions of probation, 'it shall order the expungement' — so the application states the operative facts and requests the order, and argues nothing.

primaryStatutoryAuthority.description: After a period of not less than one year beginning to run immediately on the expiration of the term of probation, the person may apply to the court for an order expunging all official records of the arrest, trial and conviction, except those maintained by the Division of Motor Vehicles; a person previously convicted of a felony may not make that motion; objections are filed within 30 days of service, and if objections are filed the court holds a hearing and, if it determines there was no serious or repeated violation of the conditions of probation, it shall order the expungement.
The clock: not less than one year, beginning to run immediately upon the expiration of the term of probation. It runs from the expiration of probation, not from the dismissal.

The predicate the submission rests on: the court, without entering a judgment of guilt, deferred further proceedings and placed the participant on probation conditioned on successful completion of the Motor Vehicle Alcohol Test and Lock Program under § 17C-5A-3a.

The hard limit on the relief requested: no Division of Motor Vehicles record may be expunged by virtue of any order entered pursuant to § 17C-5-2b, and subsection (g)(1) itself excepts records maintained by the Division of Motor Vehicles. Carried so the application never asks for relief the section withholds.

qaProhibitedTermsNote: Four groups, each for a distinct sourced reason. (1) 'petition' and 'petitioner': every West Virginia Judiciary expungement form catalogued in the committed state pack and named in the compiled profile is a petition or motion under § 61-11-25 or § 61-11-26 — a different statute with a different fee regime, a different service list, a once-per-lifetime limit under § 61-11-26(o), and an express § 61-11-26b bar on expunging DUI convictions. Section 17C-5-2b says the defendant may MOVE the court and the person may APPLY to the court, and the registry names the instruments a motion and an application. A document styling itself a petition would read as the § 61-11-26 packet the participant must not be sold. (2) 'seal', 'sealed', 'sealing': sealing of court records is the § 61-11-26 remedy — the profile records that on a granted § 61-11-26 order the court orders court records sealed and agency records expunged. Section 17C-5-2b(g) speaks only of expunging official records and says nothing about sealing. (3) 'destroy', 'destroyed', 'destruction', 'erase': the committed state pack's own never-say list forbids telling a participant that this destroys every record or that no one can ever see it again, and the profile records that legally authorised criminal-history checks and law-enforcement-type job applications can still reach expunged convictions. (4) 'pardon', 'vacate', 'vacatur', 'acquittal', 'acquitted', 'pretrial diversion', 'deferred adjudication': each names a different West Virginia route — § 5-1-16a pardon relief, § 61-14-9 trafficking vacatur, the § 61-11-25 acquittal/dismissal motion on SCA-C903, § 61-11-22 pretrial diversion (from which DUI is expressly excluded) and § 61-11-22a deferred adjudication. A § 17C-5-2b deferral is none of them, and using their vocabulary would misdescribe the relief and blur the routing boundary. Scope: these terms are prohibited in the RENDERED DOCUMENT TEXT of this component only. Several of them necessarily appear in participant-facing routing and disclosure copy, where they do necessary work — telling the participant that this is not the conviction-expungement route and that an expunged record is still reachable by legally authorised checks.

counselFlags.statement: No West Virginia Judiciary form exists for either the § 17C-5-2b(c) motion to dismiss or the § 17C-5-2b(g) application to expunge. The Court Forms index was read at source on 2026-08-06 and publishes exactly five expungement forms — SCA-C900, SCA-C903, SCA-C906, SCA-C907 and SCA-C912 — none of which is a § 17C-5-2b filing; the committed state pack catalogues the same five and ties each to § 61-11-25 or § 61-11-26. On that basis the controlling review's build blocker is answered in the negative and every court document in this route is a custom pleading. Whether an unpublished local form is used in some courts was not tested.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: Whether any court uses an unpublished local form for a § 17C-5-2b filing.

counselFlags.statement: Section 17C-5-2b(g)(1) contains a proviso, not recorded in the controlling legal review, that a person previously convicted of a felony may not make the expungement motion. The registry records it as a participant question added on this route as it is on § 61-11-25. This route treats the felony bar as excluding unit 2 (the application to expunge) only, and not unit 1 (the motion to dismiss), because the proviso sits in subsection (g).
counselFlags.mustConfirm: Confirm the felony bar is screened as a threshold question on this route, and that it bars only the subsection (g) expungement and not the subsection (c) dismissal.

counselFlags.statement: The one-year window in § 17C-5-2b(g)(1) runs from the expiration of the term of probation, not from the dismissal. The two dates are usually different and the dismissal is the more visible one, so the wrong date is the obvious failure mode. The registry requires written confirmation of the probation-expiry date from the supervising probation office or the clerk, and requires the participant's own answer to be checked against it. This route computes nothing: it states the participant's two dates side by side and never asserts that the year has run.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That any waiting-period computation downstream measures from probation expiry, never from the dismissal date.

counselFlags.statement: Hard limit that must be disclosed: no Division of Motor Vehicles record may be expunged by virtue of an order entered pursuant to this section. Subsection (g)(1) itself excepts records maintained by the Division of Motor Vehicles, and § 61-11-25(a) says so independently. The criminal record can be cleared; the driving record cannot. A participant who is chiefly concerned about the driving record is a self-help stop condition, because this route never clears it.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That the driving-record limit is disclosed before any document is produced, and that a driving-record-motivated participant is routed out.

counselFlags.statement: What LegalEase cannot complete: the court's finding on probation violations. If objections are filed within 30 days of service of the § 17C-5-2b(g) application, the court holds a hearing affording all parties an opportunity to be heard on whether there was any serious or repeated violation of the conditions of probation, and automated assistance ends there. Anyone alleging such a violation, and any objection that produces a hearing, is a self-help stop condition. Nothing in this route predicts an objection, a hearing, or how the court will find.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That an objection or an alleged probation violation ends automated assistance rather than producing further documents.

counselFlags.statement: The notice line on the subsection (g) application carries a hearing date, and the registry lists it as a manual completion item because "a hearing is held only if objections are filed, and the court sets the date." It is left blank. Nothing in this route asserts that a hearing will or will not be held, states a hearing date, or predicts an outcome.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: Whether the application should carry a notice line at all where no objection has yet been filed, and what a West Virginia court expects on it.

counselFlags.statement: The two stages must never be merged into one filing. The registry models them as separate units because the required contents, the timing and the legal effect all differ: the subsection (c) motion needs the defendant's affidavit and the Division of Motor Vehicles certification and produces dismissal and discharge without adjudication of guilt; the subsection (g) application cannot be made until a further year has run from the expiration of probation, is barred outright by any prior felony conviction, and produces expungement of the criminal record. Unit 1 must have produced a dismissal before unit 2 becomes available at all. The words expunge, expunged and expungement are prohibited in the unit-1 document text for exactly this reason.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That the pipeline cannot emit the subsection (g) application at the same time as the subsection (c) motion, and that stageNeeded gates which components are produced.

counselFlags.statement: Whether relief under § 17C-5-2b counts against the once-per-lifetime limit in § 61-11-26(o) is unsettled. Section 61-11-26(o) reaches only §§ 61-11-26 and 61-11-26a on its face, and § 17C-5-2b was read in full at source on 2026-08-06 and contains no cross-reference to it. The textual reading is that they are separate limits in separate statutes, but a participant deciding whether to spend their one lifetime conviction petition needs a settled answer. No participant copy in this route tells the participant either way.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: Whether relief under § 17C-5-2b counts against the § 61-11-26(o) once-per-lifetime limit.

counselFlags.statement: Subsection (f) makes four categories ineligible for dismissal and discharge under the section: any prosecution in which any violation of any other provision of article 17C-5 has been charged; any person holding a commercial driver's licence or operating commercial motor vehicles; any person previously having had a licence revoked for an offence with the same elements under a municipal ordinance of this state or any other state or a statute of the United States or any other state; and any person as to whom a court entered an order finding a refusal of the secondary chemical test under § 17C-5-7a. Subsection (e) allows only one discharge and dismissal under the section. Each is screened as a hard exclusion and each is a self-help stop condition; none is asserted as satisfied in any drafted document.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That each subsection (f) bar and the one-discharge limit are screened before any document is produced.

counselFlags.statement: A person as to whom dismissal and discharge have been effected is not guilty of perjury, false swearing or otherwise giving a false statement by reason of failing to disclose the arrest or trial, EXCEPT in response to an inquiry made in connection with a subsequent offence under § 17C-5-2. The exception has to travel with the protection wherever the protection is stated. Separately, the committed state pack's own never-say list forbids telling a participant that expungement destroys every record, that no one can ever see it again, or that they never have to disclose it anywhere; and the profile records that law-enforcement-type job applicants and legally required background checks may still reach expunged convictions.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That the subsequent-offence exception is carried in every participant statement of the disclosure protection.

The compiled profile's own intake checklist records West Virginia courts as "circuit, magistrate, municipal". The circuit-court destination the state pack states is for §§ 61-11-25 and 61-11-26 filings and is NOT imported here. Every court name in this route is a token filled only from the participant's own answer; no court name, court level or clerk address is prefilled.

counselFlags.statement: The instruments on this route are a motion (subsection (c): "the defendant may move the court") and an application (subsection (g): "the person may apply to the court"), and the registry names them exactly that. Every West Virginia Judiciary expungement form is a petition or motion under § 61-11-25 or § 61-11-26 — a different statute, with a different fee regime, a different service list, a once-per-lifetime limit, and an express bar on expunging DUI convictions. The words petition and petitioner are therefore prohibited in this route's rendered document text so the product can never read as a § 61-11-26 packet.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: The label a West Virginia court expects on each submission, and whether 'Applicant' is acceptable on the subsection (g) application.

counselFlags.statement: Service on the prosecuting attorney is what starts the 30-day objection window on both submissions, and it is the participant's own act. The registry lists the prosecuting attorney's street address and the certificate-of-service date and signature as manual completion items, to be completed by the participant from the current published address, because the certificate attests to what the participant actually did. No prosecutor name, no prosecutor address, no service date and no prosecutor position is ever prefilled, and no drafted document asserts that service was completed or that the prosecuting attorney did or did not object.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: The manner of service a West Virginia court accepts for each submission, and the form of the certificate.

counselFlags.statement: Section 17C-5-2b charges no fee for either motion, but subsection (h) provides that a person whose case is disposed of under the section must pay the court costs that could be assessed against a person convicted of the offence, and payment may already have been made a condition of probation. No source read for this track states an amount, and the fee figures the committed state pack does record — the § 61-11-26 civil-filing fee and the $100 State Police processing fee — belong to the conviction-expungement route and are NOT imported here. The registry records the fee waiver as "none stated in § 17C-5-2b." No amount, no waiver and no fee promise appears anywhere in this route's participant copy.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: What court costs subsection (h) produces in practice, whether any waiver exists, and whether the $100 State Police processing fee attaches to a § 17C-5-2b(g) order.

counselFlags.statement: The compiled WV profile never mentions § 17C-5-2b, the Motor Vehicle Alcohol Test and Lock Program or § 17C-5A-3a, and none of its seven pathways is this one. Worse for routing, the committed state pack states flatly that "DUI convictions cannot be expunged" and that DUI under § 17C-5-2 is excluded from pretrial diversion. Both statements are true of the routes they describe — § 61-11-26b bars expunging DUI convictions and § 61-11-22 excludes DUI from pretrial diversion — and both would turn away exactly the participant this track exists for, whose proceedings were deferred under § 17C-5-2b without any judgment of guilt being entered. Every legal proposition in this route comes from the pinned registry entry.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That the West Virginia routing table sends a completed-deferral participant to this track and not to the "DUI cannot be expunged" dead end the profile and state pack state for the conviction route.

APPLICATION FOR AN ORDER EXPUNGING ALL OFFICIAL RECORDS OF THE ARREST, TRIAL AND CONVICTION PURSUANT TO W. VA. CODE § 17C-5-2b(g). Styled an application, never a petition — the subsection says the person may apply to the court, and every West Virginia Judiciary expungement petition belongs to a different statute.

Container only, and only for the facts the registry's own generationRequirements collect: that the court deferred the proceedings and imposed probation on a stated date; the probation term; that the Motor Vehicle Alcohol Test and Lock Program was successfully completed on a stated date; that the charges were dismissed and the participant discharged on a stated date; the date the probation term expired; that the participant has no prior felony conviction; and their answers to the subsection (f) screening questions and to whether anyone has alleged a breach of the conditions of probation. Sections 61-11-25 (as a route) and 61-11-26 are not cited as authority for the relief: this application does not arise under either.

An order expunging all official records of the arrest, trial and conviction, EXCEPT those maintained by the Division of Motor Vehicles — the subsection's own words, including its own exception, so the application can never be read as asking for the driving record. No custodian is named and nothing is requested about what any agency must do, because the section names none.

This config sets usesCounty:false and carries the county through the {county} token. The renderer should separate 'this jurisdiction uses a county line' from 'this jurisdiction is Pennsylvania'.

adapterDefects.observed: courtName and courtCaption carry a {court} token so the court identification comes wholly from the participant's own answer. The renderer has no {court} substitution and no way to express 'court level unknown'.
adapterDefects.requiredAdapterBehavior: Add a {court} substitution driven by the participant's chargeCourtAndCounty answer, rendering nothing when it is blank. The court must never be synthesised or defaulted to circuit court.

adapterDefects.observed: courtCaption carries a {caseNumberLine} token because both submissions go into the existing criminal case rather than opening a new one. The renderer has no such substitution.
adapterDefects.requiredAdapterBehavior: Add a case-number line driven by caseData.docketNumber, rendering nothing when it is blank. The case number must never be synthesised.

adapterDefects.observed: The renderer's parties block is built around a sovereign party and role.
adapterDefects.requiredAdapterBehavior: No party structure is stated for a § 17C-5-2b submission and none is invented here. The adapter needs a no-opposing-party variant.

adapterDefects.observed: The certificate-of-service component is rendered once with the subsection (c) motion and again with the subsection (g) application, with a different served-document title and a different movant role each time. The renderer has no notion of a stage.
adapterDefects.requiredAdapterBehavior: Accept a stage parameter driving the served-document title and the movant role, from the participant's stageNeeded answer. Neither may be defaulted.

rendererCompatibility.fixtureShapeNote: Fixture partyData uses the renderer's own field names (petitionerName, petitionerAddress, otherNamesUsed) so that fixtures are valid PleadingRenderInput. The role label is set by presentation.movantRole, not by the fixture key name; the key name is the renderer's, and the word petitioner is prohibited in rendered output.

provenance.profileSilenceNote: The compiled WV profile contains no occurrence of '17C-5-2b', 'Test and Lock', '17C-5A-3a' or any DUI-deferral pathway. Its only occurrences of '17C-5-2' are the single repeated statement that DUI under 17C-5-2 is excluded from pretrial diversion under 61-11-22. The seven pathways it enumerates are the 61-11-25 no-conviction route, 61-11-26 conviction expungement, the 61-11-26a accelerated route, the 60A-4-407 conditional discharge, 5-1-16a pardon relief, 61-14-9 trafficking vacatur and juvenile relief. This route therefore rests on the pinned registry entry; the profile and the committed state pack are used only for the West Virginia court-level, form-catalogue, intake-field and terminology facts they do record.

stageNote: Stage two of a sequential two-stage route. Cannot be produced until stage one has produced a dismissal and discharge and a further year has run from the expiration of probation. Barred outright by any prior felony conviction.

The gap is carried as a counsel flag rather than filled — the handling the ND config applies to its own missing verification statute.
